reviews.title: 1 Star — Very Disappointing and Misleading Experience
reviews.text:
⭐ 1 Star — Very Disappointing and Misleading Experience

I’m extremely disappointed with BetterMe. I purchased multiple programs, including the Attachment Style course, which was actually the one I was most excited about. After paying for everything, I discovered I couldn’t even access the programs I purchased.

When I contacted customer support, I was told that only one program can be set as the main program on an account at a time. Apparently, because my account was set to Calisthenics, I couldn’t access the Attachment Style course or AI Companion.

How does that make any sense? Why allow customers to purchase multiple programs if they can’t access what they’ve paid for? This should be clearly explained before taking someone’s money.

I ended up canceling my subscriptions out of frustration. It’s incredibly disappointing because I was genuinely excited to use these programs.

I strongly encourage BetterMe to rethink this system. Customers shouldn’t have to contact support just to switch between programs they’ve already purchased. It’s inconvenient, misleading, and feels like a complete waste of money.

I’m very unhappy with my experience and would caution others to understand exactly what they’re paying for before subscribing.

reviews.title: No refunds
reviews.text:
The app itself is reasonably well designed and easy to use, but unfortunately, I can’t say the workouts have delivered any particularly significant results for me.

However, my biggest disappointment is the company’s approach to subscriptions and refunds. I hadn’t used the app for several weeks, yet £99 was automatically debited from my account without any prior warning or notification that the renewal was approaching or that payment was about to be taken.

Having subsequently contacted customer support, my request for a refund was refused. I find this extremely disappointing and, frankly, poor customer service. Automatically renewing subscriptions without a courtesy reminder, particularly when a substantial payment is involved, feels unnecessarily misleading and leaves customers paying for a service they are no longer using.

A well-designed app should be matched by a fair and transparent subscription policy. Unfortunately, this experience has left me with a very negative impression of the company, and I would urge anyone considering signing up to be extremely cautious of the auto-renewal terms.

reviews.title: Poor customer service
reviews.text:
I signed up to the initial 3 month programme. I found the app useful. The content was good it was easy to use and I was generally happy with it. 
I wasn’t going to continue using it beyond the 3 months just because I had learned some bits about myself I felt I didn’t need to be ‘managed’ any more. I did use the app for a good couple of weeks initially and then I just didn’t see the need for it. 
At the end of my 3 month programme I needed to cancel the subscription. I asked to cancel it on the same day as it renewed. So the company decided to give me back half my money and keep the other half even though they know o am not going to use the app.  Customer services were very dismissive and feel like this was fair and particularly as I had agreed to the reimbursement. 
It isn’t fair. It is simply that I would rather lose £47 than £94. You have still taken £47 for absolutely nothing. 
 Customer service is lacking somewhat. 

Looking at the reviews, I’m not the first person and dare say I won’t be the last. Taking money for nothing in the current climate. 

Be aware…

reviews.title: Misleading Subscription Offer and Refund Refusal
reviews.text:
I accidentally clicked on what appeared to be a promotional offer email and was immediately charged for a subscription. I contacted customer support right away and was told the subscription would be canceled. It wasn’t.
I followed up by email, expecting them to correct the mistake, but instead they hid behind their refund policy and refused to issue a refund. The entire process felt misleading and dishonest.
There are many better apps online that offer similar features for free. In my opinion, this app relies on confusing offers and aggressive subscription tactics to make money rather than providing real value.
I eventually had to dispute the charge through my bank. The situation became so complicated that my bank informed me they would be closing my account because of what they considered suspicious activity related to this transaction. At that point, I felt like my financial information and account security were being put at risk.
I’ve deleted the app and unsubscribed from all of their marketing emails. I’m leaving this review to warn others: be extremely careful before clicking on any offer or trial because canceling and getting a refund may not be as straightforward as you expect.

reviews.title: Watch out for membership fees!!!
reviews.text:
I signed up and chose my workouts for a fee of £38. I then signed up to a monthly subscription for £6.99. I decided it wasn’t for me and cancelled my subscription via my Apple Pay account (where it lists all subscriptions) and deleted the App. Little did I know that the £38 was not a one-off cost, but actually a separate monthly membership fee. This did not show up my usual list of subscriptions (via Apple account) but only visible via their app which is very sneaky! This was not clear when I signed up and I can see now other reviews reporting similar things. There is no warning they are going to take payment (of course not, why would they do that? That would give you a chance to cancel wouldn’t it?) .
Customer service is non existent and I logged a complaint via ‘help with app’. I then got a generic email response stating that I was not entitled to a refund. They only offer refunds if you can prove that the workouts have not worked for you and you can’t see any visible results within a certain time period! 

Why are there 2 separate monthly subscriptions?? I also wonder how much money they make from users who have been stung in the same way? Utter rip off and would AVOID!!!!


JUST TO ADD- I’ve also read some review responses from BetterMe who state they are ‘transparent’!! If that were the case then there wouldn’t be an issue about fees now would there?!!!

reviews.title: So many problems and customer service really unhelpful
reviews.text:
The idea seems good but the technology doesn’t support it - workouts may or may not play and may or may not log once complete; calorie tracker is painfully slow and often doesn’t register what you put in - if you have a wrapper for something and use the barcode scanner, the nutritional info the tracker logs for it doesn’t always match what’s on the wrapper (that’s if it logs at all).  Voiceover, timers etc for the workouts aren’t always in sync with the video - really frustrating and confusing when you’re trying to do the work out.

I’m not convinced customer service isn’t just AI replying to emails.  Same response (some variation of turn your phone off and on again or you need to complete the questionnaire at the end of the workout or you need a stable internet connection - none of which actually fix any of the problems) phrased a slightly different way over and over.

Overall it’s just a huge headache

reviews.title: Took £100 without warning – left me with £15 to live on
reviews.text:
Took £100 without warning – left me with £15 to live on

I signed up to this app in February on a discounted trial (around £30). I’m very careful with subscriptions, and I’m confident I cancelled straight away to avoid any auto-renewal.

Today I checked my bank account and discovered I only have £15 left to last the next three weeks — because this company has taken £100 without my knowledge.

I have not used the app, and I was completely unaware that:

* the subscription was still active
* it would auto-renew
* the renewal price would be nearly £100

Customer services claim I was sent emails outlining the renewal and cost. I have checked thoroughly — inbox, junk, deleted — and I did not receive these emails.

Despite explaining the situation, they have refused a refund and simply insist the emails must have been sent. That is not good enough.

A quick search online shows many other customers reporting the same issue, which raises serious concerns about how transparent this company’s billing practices are.

I have now had to:

* cancel my card
* remove Apple Pay
* raise a dispute with my bank

This has caused significant stress and left me in a very difficult financial position.

Avoid.

reviews.title: Workouts have bugs
reviews.text: Have been using for 2 weeks now and every daily workout is so buggy. The timer is constantly lagging, along with the chimes to tell you when to move on to next activity and a few times the whole app has crashed in the middle of my workout losing my progress right when I’m in the middle. This is so so frustrating. The app also totally drains my phone battery when it’s doing a workout and my phone gets really hot. Will not be renewing subscription once my current month is up. If you can’t work out effectively then much of the health benefits are lost. I also find a bug regularly that it lags when I try to switch views from “progress” to “plan” to “other” on the menus. A real shame as this app has some great potential. It’s just so so buggy.

reviews.title: Shady as hell business
reviews.text:
It is an extremely expensive app. They do not give numbers of sets or reps for each exercise they want you to perform. You can pause, yes, but each section is meant to be timed and moves too rapidly with each one only allowing for about 30 secs. Not to mention that half of the time you are supposed to be doing the exercise, they are explaining how to do it so you loose half the time anyways! It is not beginner friendly and I would never recommend this to anyone. For the price they charge, just get a trainer or look up free videos online. Waste of money and even if you delete the app after one training they refuse to refund people. Infuriating!

Update!!
 I am still trying to get my refund from the shady as hell business. They offered me a partial refund and an extension—of no charge—on the app that I told them I would not be using. I accept both because at this point I just wanted at least some of the money I spent back since I have no intention of using the app. Thank goodness I had my card lock! Because they attempted to charge me what they said they were going to refund me then I receive an email saying that they could not process my refund because my bank declined it. Yeah my bank declined it because you tried to charge me you stupid shady as hell app

reviews.title: Meal tracker is poor
reviews.text:
The meal tracking functionality is badly designed. There is no indication that you have already logged a meal, so it’s easy to accidentally log one twice. Then there’s no way of removing the meal within the app. I found a way of doing this in the browser version but in the app the calories have not reduced. 
In app support chat goes to an email which then eventually directs you to the FAQs.
So glad I waited it out before sign up and qualified for the 90% discount, as would be very disappointed if I’d paid full price. Constant upselling is also annoying, maybe wait a while before bombarding new users with requests for more cash. It needs to improve a whole lot if I am going to consider keeping it after my initial period ends

reviews.title: Scammer
reviews.text: I paid £15, for a trial, NEVER even ended up opening the app due to being ill. I was not made aware this was a subscription, never received a confirmation email or anything. A month later I’m charged £37. I’m on maternity leave so can’t afford to throw money away. Trying to speak to help and they’re saying I have to had done 5 workouts to get a refund? Under the law, if it’s a hidden subscription, I am wholly entitled to a refund, and the help desk are using every excuse to not refund and just wanting to upgrade my package instead of giving me money back. I haven’t used the app ONCE, which works more in my favour, as if i’d have used the app, I’d realistically be less entitled to a refund as opposed to NEVER using the app. Hidden subscription’s are illegal and legal action is being taken
